newsitem.title: FRANCE: French companies in Chinese power plant deal.
newsitem.headline: French companies in Chinese power plant deal.

text.p: French state-owned electricity utility EDF and GEC Alsthom said on Monday they had signed a deal to build and operate the first Chinese power station entirely financed by foreign investment.
The total value of the project exceeded three billion francs ($589.9 million), said Electricite de France and GEC Alsthom, which formed a consortium to carry out the project.
"This is China's first BOT -- build, operate and transfer -- project and will be entirely financed by foriegn capital," the companies said in a statement.
EDF will hold 60 percent of the company set up for the project while GEC Alsthom will hold 40 percent.
EDF chairman Edmond Alphandery called Laibin B "an innovative project which will serve as a reference for foreign investment in power stations in China".
The agreement for the finance, construction and operation of the 2x350 megawatt Laibin "B" coal-fired power station was signed with authorities of the province of Guangxi in Beijing on Monday.

The consortium will finance and build the power station. After completion in 1999, it will operate the station commercially for 15 years, receiving revenues from the sale of power. The station will then be transferred to the government.
China is the largest market in the world for electricity production and its needs are growing at the rate of eight percent a year, the companies said.

GEC Alsthom, a joint venture between General Electric Plc of Britain and Alcatel Alsthom of France, will be the consortium leader for construction of the plant and will supply the turbine generators, boilers and electrical equipment.
Laibin represents EDF's first involvement in a major thermal power generation project and will also constitute its first investment in Asia. ($ = 5.086 French Francs)
